question: what fraction of typical pretraining tokens are machine-checkable (strong verification: execution/tests/answers)?
method: sample-level probes via HF datasets-server API + mixture-weighted extrapolation; first-cut, n=20 per corpus

probes.HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu sample-10BT: 0/20 machine-checkable (natural web text, no verifier possible)
probes.nvidia/Nemotron-SFT-Agentic-v2 tool_call: tool responses carry structured success/status fields -> step-level checkable in principle
probes.mbpp: API probe 404; known test-included corpus (~100% by construction)
probes.bigcode/the-stack-smol: gated (401); code-with-tests fraction not directly sampled this cut

yield_estimate.note: ~5-6% of a standard pretraining mixture is strongly machine-checkable (math 5% + code-with-tests ~0.5%); executable-but-untested code adds weak verification only

headline: only ~5% of the standard pretraining universe carries machine-verifiable signal - and agentic/tool corpora are the one class that can be ~100% step-verified, which is exactly where Hebri's verified trajectories live
caveats: first-cut: n=20 probes, mixture weights are representative not measured, code-tests fraction estimated from literature (~2-4% of GitHub tokens are test files); full census = larger sampling + direct stack access
